content.text: Fabre describes Eumenes and Osmia nest-building, provisioning, larval safety, sex determination, and experiments showing mothers adjust offspring sex to available cell size. He examines Glow-worms, which anesthetize and liquefy snails, adhere to surfaces, and produce controlled light. He details cabbage-caterpillar feeding and Microgaster parasitism. The diary then recounts Carrie and Anna’s movements between their Canandaigua home, church, school, Seminary, Academy, gardens, Sucker Brook, Penn Yan, Victor, Utica, New York, Buffalo, Niagara Falls, and relatives’ homes. It records studies, friendships, religious life, social events, Civil War patriotism, soldiers’ departures, battles, deaths, Lincoln’s assassination, emancipation, family marriages, Grandfather Beals’s death, and charitable work for soldiers and freedpeople.
